questions.def: Future perfect indicates completion before a future point.
questions.question: By the time we arrive, they ___ all the food.

questions.def: Present perfect 'have seen' implies completed action with relevance now.
questions.question: I ___ that movie three times already.

questions.def: Use 'will have graduated' for an action completed before a future point.
questions.question: By this time next year, she will be graduated and starts her new job.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous for action started in the past and continuing.
questions.question: He ___ here since he graduated.

questions.def: 'Was going to' expresses an unfulfilled intention in the past.
questions.question: I ___ to call you yesterday, but I forgot.

questions.def: 'Were' is used in the second conditional for hypothetical situations.
questions.question: If I ___ you, I would apologize.

questions.def: Future perfect continuous: 'will have been living'.
questions.question: By next year, I am living here for five years.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous emphasizes the duration of the waiting.
questions.question: I ___ for the bus for an hour!

questions.def: 'Would' is the past form of 'will' in reported speech.
questions.question: She said she ___ come to the party.

questions.def: Past perfect ('had already') for an action completed before another past action.
questions.question: He ___ finished the report when I arrived.

questions.def: After 'did', use the base form of the verb (see).
questions.question: I didn't saw the accident yesterday.

questions.def: Past continuous ('were studying') for an ongoing action in the past.
questions.question: They ___ while I was cooking dinner.

questions.def: Past perfect 'had left' shows completion before another past event.
questions.question: The train ___ before we got to the station.

questions.def: 'Had' expresses a regret about a past situation.
questions.question: I wish I ___ more time to travel.

questions.def: Use 'for' with duration; 'since' with a specific starting point.
questions.question: She is working on the project since last week.

questions.def: Present perfect continuous emphasizes the duration and continuation.
questions.question: We ___ in this city for five years now.

questions.def: Future perfect emphasizes completion before a future time.
questions.question: By this time tomorrow, I ___ finished packing.

questions.def: Simple past ('went') for a completed action in the past.
questions.question: He ___ to the gym every day last year.

questions.def: 'Going to' is followed by the base form of the verb (visit).
questions.question: They are going to visiting their grandparents.

questions.def: Simple past ('met') for a completed action at a specific time.
questions.question: I ___ him yesterday at the conference.

questions.def: Present perfect 'have known' for a state that started in the past.
questions.question: I ___ him since we were children.

questions.def: Past continuous ('was sleeping') for an interrupted action.
questions.question: She ___ when the phone rang.

questions.def: 'Know' is a stative verb; avoid continuous tenses.
questions.question: He has been knowing about it for years.

questions.def: Simple past ('rained') for a completed action in the past.
questions.question: It ___ all day yesterday.

questions.def: Third conditional: 'would have gone' for hypothetical past.
questions.question: I ___ to the gym if I hadn't been so tired.

questions.def: Past continuous in reported speech, 'was coming'.
questions.question: He told me he ___ coming to the meeting.

questions.def: Use 'for' with a duration of time, not 'since'.
questions.question: She has been living here since three months.

questions.def: Simple past for a completed action at a specific time.
questions.question: They ___ the project last week.

questions.def: Past perfect for an action completed before another past action.
questions.question: The movie ___ by the time we arrived at the cinema.

questions.def: 'Am going to' for planned future action.
questions.question: I ___ to Paris next summer.
